INDIANAPOLIS 46266
1330 West Michigan Street 633-4420
November 15, 1971
Mr. Daniel S. Tankersley
Prosecuting Attorney
59th Judicial Circuit of Indiana
Winamac, Indiana 46996
STREAM POLLUTION CONTROL BOARD
Dear Mr. Tankersley:
Re: Aerial Application of Herbicide for
Marijuana Eradication
Newton, Pulaski, St. Joseph and
Starke Counties
This acknowledges your letter dated November 5, 1971, concerning aerial application of 2, 4-D granules for eradication of wild-growing marijuana in Pulaski County under a Criminal Justice Planning Agency grant.
On November 11, members of the staff met with Mr. John L. Clarke, Jr., of Clarke Outdoor Spraying Company, Inc., LaGrange, Illinois, with whom you have contracted for the aerial application. Mr. Clarke explained that dry granules of 20 percent 2,4-D (an ester) would be applied from 2 orifices under each of 2 tanks at a rate of 4 pounds/acre 2, 4-D (20 pounds/acre granules) at a height of 35 feet at 40 mph resulting in a 20-foot swath. Application would be cut off while passing over power lines and one pass would be made over ditches less than 20 feet wide.
Mr. Clarke further explained that the granules had a 20-30 day release rate and that application would be made in May.
From the above information, we believe that the herbicide could be applied as described without having a direct toxic effect on aquatic life. However, residual effects have not yet been evaluated. Moreover, since some areas of application are in or near State wildlife refuges, particularly in Newton County, we referred Mr. Clarke to the Fish and Game Division of the Department of Natural Resources.
When the two agencies have had time to evaluate all of the ecological aspects of the proposed program, you will be informed of any recommendations.
truly yours,
Technidal Secretary
Perry E. Miller
